Can these be added as `Bios Attributes` in the PLDM repository? These attributes can be made D-Bus backed, allowing them to be associated with D-Bus properties.

Do you see any additional advantages in adding this support within the bios-settings-mgr repository?

Thanks a lot Archana for the review. 
Currently `BIOS Attributes` can be obtained via various ways PLDM, ipmi or redfish host interface. 
If `SecureBoot` properties are made as part of bios attributes then bmcweb shall have to implement parsing logic to obtain `SecureBoot` properties. 
Adding the change to bios-settings-manager will help us query the properties via dbus. 
There is a dedicated schema for Remote UEFI secure boot configuration (https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/SecureBoot.v1_1_2.json).
do you have any work in progress commit in bmcweb that exposes this properties in redfish ? if not redfish who sets these properties on your systems ?

On NVIDIA systems, the bios sets the values via redfish host interface(first boot). 
And also users can perform patch to change the value which will be picked by bios in the upcoming boot.

> On NVIDIA systems, the bios sets the values via redfish host interface(first boot).

Can you explain a little bit more on how this is done? does your bios firmware has network/redfish stack ? 

> And also users can perform patch to change the value which will be picked by bios in the upcoming boot.

Also, looks like there is no bios support in bmcweb yet, is that something that you plan to upstream ? are there WIP commits that are in progress ? 

And also the secureboot schema - is that already implemented in bmcweb ? or are there commits that are in review for this ? I just want to make sure that what ever back end we did , that should be consumable by redfish.

During the bios boot, BIOS sends ipmi commands(oem as well as spec defined). 
https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0270_1.3.0.pdf
Through oem commands bios will get BMCs network information. As per redfish host interface spec bios-bmc can be connected by internal network such as USB Network Interface.
Through ipmi group command as defined in above spec, bios will request for bootstrap account. This account will be used by bios for redfish communication. 
The account will be deleted in following cases
1) bmcweb service restarts
2) host reset is detected
Once bios has the credentials, bios can perform GET/POST/PATCH/PUT operations. 
Bios can PUT the biosAttributes information to BMC via redfish.
Bios can PATCH SecureBoot information via redfish.
 
Once the data is available in BMC, user can perform the patch operation which will be taken by bios in the next boot. 
bios performs get on bios/Settings URI to check if there is any information changed as defined in bios-settings-manager.
